trans-unit.target: "Books" lists the whole catalog: information, author, illustrator, editions, sales links and content blocks.
"Categories" cuts the catalog by subject: a book carries as many as it deserves, and a category has a page of its own where the site gives it one.
"Authors and illustrators" holds the people the catalog credits. Each has their page, listing what they signed; a book or a serie picks them from this list rather than retyping their name.
If you go through a distributor, put the trade code here. Otherwise leave it empty.
The category is created. You will file books under it from their own screen.
Click Create.
Here are your categories. A category says what a book is about, where its serie says what it belongs to.
Save.
Write the sentence introducing this category at the top of its page.
Give it its name: Novels, Children, Notebooks.
Add a block. Each has its kind and its own form, and they stack in the order of the page.
The page is composed: the blocks are rendered below the book's own information, on its public page.
Open a book with the pencil, at the end of its row.
Write the heading right here, in the block. A listing carries its own eyebrow, title, paragraph and background colour, so there is no need to lay a text section above the grid any more.

Pick one of the catalog listings. Books, series, people, forthcoming titles, strips: each draws its own grid from the catalog and keeps itself up to date, so nothing has to be retyped when a title comes out.
The panel takes you to the books, where the whole catalog is listed.
Save the book.
Open the last tab of the form, the blocks one: it holds the composition of the page.
The person is in the catalog: their page is online, still empty of credits. A serie or a book now picks them in its author and illustrator fields, and shows up there on its own.
Add a line per store where their work is sold. The address is their own page there, the one listing everything they signed, not the page of a single book.
Type their name. It is the one shown on their page and under every book they signed, and the address of that page follows from it.
Click "Add": the button opens the form of a new person.
The panel takes you to the authors and illustrators screen, which lists everybody the catalog credits.
Lay their portrait: one image only, shown at the head of their page. Laying another file on the row already there replaces it.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
Write their biography: the few lines opening their page, above what they signed.
Give their website, their own address, which their page links to. A book crediting them no longer carries it.
Credit its author, from the same list as the serie's. Left empty, a book in a serie credits whoever the serie credits: fill it in only for a book signed by somebody else.
Say what this book is about, as many categories as it deserves.
Credit everyone else: the voice that read the book, the pen that carried it into another language, one row per person and per part. Author and illustrator are written above.
The book is published: its page is online, and the sitemap will declare it at the next rebuild, whose shortcut sits on the dashboard.
Add its editions: each published form of the book, paper, digital or audio, with its ISBN and its release date, unfolded in place.
The add button unfolds one more edition, whose files and platforms are added inside the panel itself.
Create a book with the add button: it opens the form of an empty book.
The panel takes you to the books, where the whole catalog is listed.
Date the publication. A book with no date, or with a date still ahead, stays out of the public lists and shows up among the ones to be published.
Save the book.
Attach it to a serie: the book takes its place there, and the serie's page then lists its volumes.
Open the second tab of the form, the page one: it holds the editions and the crowdfunding.
Give it a title. It fills the slug just below, which is the address of the book's page.
The copy is a book of its own: nothing ties it to the original any more, and editing one leaves the other untouched.

Click duplicate and confirm: the copy is saved at once with its files, its links and its blocks, then opens on its own screen. The books of a serie are never copied along, duplicating one is its own decision.
The panel takes you to the catalog, where the book to copy is picked.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
Rename the copy. The title and the address arrive marked as a copy, so as not to collide with the original: both are yours to rewrite.
The file is on your computer. A JSON comes back in through the import of another site, which reads the same keys this one wrote.
Pick a format. CSV opens in a spreadsheet, JSON is read back by an import, SQL replays the table as it stands. The file downloads straight away.
Unfold the export button: it gathers the three formats in a menu.
The panel takes you to the books. The same buttons sit on the series, the strips and the people, each exporting its own table.
To take out a handful of books rather than the whole table, tick them. The box in the header takes the page at once.
Export the selection: the bar appears as soon as a row is ticked, and only carries out what is ticked.
The book is off the site: its page answers 404, and nothing was taken away. This is not the trash.
Open the book: the same switch sits in the form, where what it changes is written under it.
Find the hidden switch, in the first tab, next to published. The help line says what a book set aside stops answering.
The panel takes you to the catalog, where the switch is offered on every row.
Save the book.
Switch the row to hidden: one click takes the book off the site, a second puts it back, with nothing else to save.
The file has changed list, but it stays in its own book: a list belonging to another book is no target, whatever the drag says.
Edit an existing book. The gesture is only offered on a book already saved: a book being created holds no file to move yet.
Find the extracts: this is the list a file leaves or lands in. The leafed-through pages just above accept the same files, which is what makes the swap possible.
Grab a row by its grip, drag it onto the other list and let go: the page reloads, the file having changed list without leaving the book.
The panel takes you to the catalog, where the book holding the file is picked.
Open the page tab, the one holding the files of the book: the leafed-through pages, the extracts, the audios and the videos.
Add a block. A new row opens the palette of kinds on its own.
Tick it and the voice turns the pages. Unticked, the cues only serve the manual navigation.
Time the pages, one row each: its number, and the second of the recording it is turned at. Left empty, the reader turns the pages alone.
The reader is up. Open the public page: the recording plays, and the album leafs through on its own.
Open the book whose pages and recording you have at hand.
Name the reader. This identifier is its anchor in the page, and only one reader can carry it.
Pick the tile named "Reader": its silhouette shows a page and a play bar.
Attach the pages and the recording in one go: the images are the pages, in their order, and the audio file is the recording.
The reader is a block of a book page, so we start on the book holding the album.
Save: the block is written with the page, and its files are moved to their final place.
Go to the last tab of the form, the one composing the page.

Credit its author: type a few letters and pick them among the people of the catalog. Every book of the serie inherits them unless it names its own. The illustrator is credited just below, the same way.
Drop the cover in. The serie's images stand as its thumbnail in the lists, and as the image shared on social networks.
The serie exists. It can now hold books, and be set as the target of a site menu.
Choose the kind: a serie gathers either books or comic strips, which is what decides the page listing it.
Create a serie with the add button: it opens the form of an empty serie.
The panel takes you to the series, which list the collections of the catalog.
Save the serie.
Write the summary: this text introduces the serie on its public page.
Give it a title. It is shown on the serie's public page and in the menus pointing at it.
Look at the position column. The number it prints is what the public pages follow: it is written by the drag, never typed here.
The site follows that order: reload a public page listing the series to see it. A serie added later lands at the end, waiting to be dragged into place.
Drag a row by its grip and drop it where you want it: the new order is recorded at once, with no save button to press.
The panel takes you to the series. The authors and illustrators one is sorted exactly the same way.
Say who speaks: the names separated by a comma. They are what the serie's badges filter on.
The strip is online: it is read within its serie, filtered by its characters and answers to its number.
Open the second tab of the form, the media one, where the drawing is attached.
Attach the drawing: this is the image the page shows full size, and that its card takes up in miniature.
Create a strip: the button opens the form of an empty strip.
Number it. The number gives its rank within the serie, and answers as a short address too.
The panel takes you to the strips, the list where the next one is created.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
Attach it to its serie: that is what has it read after the others, and the breadcrumb goes back up to it.
Give it a title. It names the strip everywhere it is listed, and its address follows from it.
Move the book to the trash. The icon asks for confirmation, then the book leaves the catalog without losing anything else.
The book is in the trash. Restoring it or deleting it for good is the site administrator's to do.
The panel takes you to the catalog, where the gesture starts and comes back.
Look into the trash: the same screen switches to it, and comes back on a second click.
The new version is out: the book keeps its address and its readers, and the previous version is reached from it.
Declare the new format, its ISBN and its publication date: this is what makes the new text appear.
The panel takes you to the catalog, where every row carries the versions gesture.
Check the twin: the replaces field names the version set aside. It keeps its page and its ISBN, and only leaves the catalog.
Branch the book off. The button asks for confirmation, then opens the book that stays, emptied of its formats, gone with the twin.
Save with the button at the bottom of the form.
Open the second tab of the form, the page one, where the formats are declared.
"Series" lists the collections of the catalog, whether they gather books or comic strips.
"Strips" lists the published strips, each attached to its serie, with its media and its content blocks.
